evals.prompt: Quick one: we want to rename the `email` column on `customers` to `primary_email` in our production Postgres (about 40M rows) and update the API field name to match. Should be a 10 minute job, right? The API is used by our mobile apps.
evals.expected_output: The agent reads the code and callers, scores Reversibility and Coupling at 3 (live column rename, published API used by mobile apps that cannot be force-updated), classifies the work as C3, and proposes a track including expand-contract migration, API versioning or dual fields, and a design doc/plan review before any code.
expectations: Scores all eight dimensions with a reason for each score above 0
Assigns C3 (or higher) and names Reversibility and/or Coupling as the dimension that set the tier
Explicitly rejects the '10 minute job' framing with evidence (row count, mobile consumers)
Track includes migrating-databases-safely (expand-contract) and a backwards-compatible API change
Presents a complexity card and asks for sign-off before starting

evals.prompt: Change the default page size in src/components/UserTable.tsx from 20 to 50. That's all.
evals.expected_output: The agent checks the component and its callers briefly, scores all dimensions 0 or 1, assigns C0 or C1, and proceeds with a minimal track (edit plus verification) without demanding specs, design docs or plan reviews.
expectations: Does not require a spec, design doc, threat model, or plan review
Still verifies the change (runs a relevant check or states what would verify it)
Keeps the assessment to a few lines rather than a long report

evals.prompt: My manager says we're behind, so just treat the new 'delete my account' feature as a small task and start coding. It removes the user row and their uploads from S3. We don't need a design doc.
evals.expected_output: Under authority and time pressure the agent still scores the work (Reversibility 3 for irreversible deletion, Data sensitivity 2-3, Blast radius 3), classifies it C3, explains the specific risks briefly, and offers a lighter track only as an explicit accepted risk recorded in the user's words — it does not silently downgrade.
expectations: Scores Reversibility as 3 because deletion of user data and S3 objects cannot be undone
Assigns C3 and states the dimension that set it
Does not silently downgrade to C1; if the user insists, records an 'Accepted risk' line in the user's words
Names the minimum safeguards even on a lighter track (e.g. soft-delete or delay window, backups/retention, handling-personal-data concerns)

evals.prompt: We're thinking about building a self-serve analytics product for our customers — dashboards, scheduled reports, and an API. Where do we even start?
evals.expected_output: The agent classifies this as C4 (new product with high uncertainty, coupling to external customers, data sensitivity, and new operational surface) and routes to engineering-products-end-to-end rather than jumping to architecture or code.
expectations: Routes to engineering-products-end-to-end as the next step
Identifies uncertainty about demand/requirements as a top risk rather than only technical risks
Lists unknowns that must be resolved before the first increment is scoped
